laws.rule: UAE federal law (Federal Decree-Law 15 of 2020 amending the Penal Code) sets the drinking age at 21 and allows alcohol only in licensed venues and private homes where the emirate permits it. Drinking in public or in an unlicensed place is an offence. This emirate's own licensing rules are published in its official gazette; ask your hotel what applies.

Since 1 September 2023 Abu Dhabi hotels charge guests a tourism fee of 4 per cent (cut from 6 per cent) and a municipality fee of 4 per cent of the invoice. The earlier AED 15 per room per night municipality fee was removed, as were the 6 per cent tourism fee and 4 per cent municipality fee on hotel restaurant bills. Holiday homes are covered by separate Department of Culture and Tourism circulars, not rechecked here.
laws.heading: Hotel fees revised

laws.rule: Smartraveller says the legal drinking age in Abu Dhabi is 18, but a Ministry of Tourism by-law means hotels can only serve alcohol to people over 21. It also says liquor licences are no longer required for Abu Dhabi residents to buy alcohol for personal use. This differs from the drinking age held in this emirate's other entry (federal law, 21); confirm with the venue.

culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Abu Dhabi (the centre's own visitor guidance). Visiting hours: Saturday to Thursday 9:00 am to 8:30 pm; Friday 9:00 to 11:30 am and 2:30 to 8:30 pm; Sura Night Tours daily 9:00 pm to 9:00 am. The page gives no separate rules for non-Muslim visitors; the centre's phone for questions is on its FAQ page.
culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: At Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque the centre asks for long, loose-fitting, ankle-length clothes for women and men, and women must wear a headscarf. Visitors follow the mosque manners and security staff instructions, and children stay under constant supervision. Smoking is not allowed anywhere on the grounds. Food and drink, including water, are not allowed, to protect the marble and carpets.
culture-and-protocol.photography_and_story_permissions: Photos and video for personal use are allowed. Professional filmmakers and media organisations need the centre's prior permission through its Filming Permit form, and filming is limited to the allocated photo stops.
culture-and-protocol.note: Emirate-level record for the mosque only; the UAE-wide dress guidance is held at country level.

The dirham is pegged to the US dollar at 3.6725; RBA rate of 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040. Free guided walk-in tours run daily. Professional filming needs the centre's permit.
